# Protocol Specification

**Authoritative wire contract.** Defined once in `protocol/p2pgpu.fbs` (R3). C++ headers are generated by `flatc` at build time into the build tree — never hand-edited, never committed.

`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1`

---

## 1. Transport and framing

### Control plane — WebSocket, binary frames only

Every control message is a FlatBuffers-encoded `Envelope`, sent as a single WebSocket **binary** frame. No text frames, no JSON on the wire.

```
offset  size  field
[0]      4    magic          0x50324750 ("P2GP") — cheap wrong-protocol rejection
[4]      2    protocol_ver   u16 LE
[6]      2    flags          u16 LE  (bit 0: payload_follows)
[8]      4    fb_len         u32 LE  — length of the FlatBuffers Envelope
[12]     N    fb_bytes       the Envelope
[12+N]   M    payload        opaque result bytes, present iff flags bit 0
```

`payload` is deliberately **outside** the FlatBuffer. Result buffers are up to 8 MiB of GPU output; keeping them out of the verified region avoids paying verification cost on bulk data whose interpretation is fully determined by `OutputSpec`.

### Reading a frame — the only sanctioned sequence (R11)

```cpp
// 1. Header is fixed-size. Reject anything shorter before touching it.
if (frame.size() < kHeaderBytes) return reject(ErrorCode::MalformedMessage);

// 2. Parse header fields from a bounds-checked span. No pointer arithmetic.
const auto hdr = ParseHeader(frame.first(kHeaderBytes));   // returns std::optional
if (!hdr) return reject(ErrorCode::MalformedMessage);
if (hdr->magic != kMagic) return reject(ErrorCode::MalformedMessage);
if (hdr->protocol_ver != PROTOCOL_VERSION) return fatal(ErrorCode::VersionMismatch);

// 3. Every declared length is checked against the frame AND against its MAX
//    before anything is allocated or indexed.
if (hdr->fb_len > kMaxEnvelopeBytes) return reject(ErrorCode::PayloadTooLarge);
if (frame.size() < kHeaderBytes + hdr->fb_len) return reject(ErrorCode::MalformedMessage);

// 4. THE VERIFIER. Nothing above this line has read a schema field.
const auto fb = frame.subspan(kHeaderBytes, hdr->fb_len);
flatbuffers::Verifier v(fb.data(), fb.size(), kMaxVerifyDepth, kMaxVerifyTables);
if (!VerifyEnvelopeBuffer(v)) return reject(ErrorCode::MalformedMessage);

// 5. Only now may fields be read.
const Envelope* env = GetEnvelope(fb.data());
```

**Deviating from this sequence is a defect regardless of whether it appears to work.** `kMaxVerifyDepth` and `kMaxVerifyTables` bound recursion and table count — FlatBuffers' defense against nesting-based resource exhaustion.

### Data plane — WebRTC DataChannel
Content-addressed asset fetch only. Chunk size **16 KiB** (safe cross-browser floor; do not assume 256 KiB EOR support). Messages are FlatBuffers `AssetMsg` unions, verified identically.

```
AssetRequest  { hash, chunk_from, chunk_to }
AssetChunk    { hash, index, total, bytes }
AssetMiss     { hash }
```

**A peer-supplied asset is untrusted input.** Verify the BLAKE3 hash of the reassembled asset before use, and bound `index`/`total` against the expected chunk count before computing any offset. Reassembly offset math uses checked arithmetic — this is the classic integer-overflow site.

Any peer fetch must fall back to `GET /asset/{hash}` on the coordinator. The system must be correct with the data plane fully disabled.

---

## 2. Schema — `protocol/p2pgpu.fbs`

Sketch of the shape. The real file is authoritative; keep this section in sync with it (`WORKFLOW.md` §6).

```fbs
namespace p2pgpu.wire;

struct Uuid   { hi: ulong; lo: ulong; }          // WorkerId / TaskId / JobId
struct Hash32 { a: ulong; b: ulong; c: ulong; d: ulong; }   // BLAKE3

enum DType : byte { U32, I32, F32, F16, Bytes }

union DeterminismClass { Exact, Tolerant, Statistical }
table Exact       {}
table Tolerant    { rel_eps: float; abs_eps: float; }
table Statistical { test: StatTest; }

table OutputSpec { bytes: uint; dtype: DType; }

table AccumulationSpec {
  upload_interval_ms: uint;    // >= 500 (invariant 6)
  min_iterations:     ulong;
}

table TaskEnvelope {
  task_id:     Uuid;
  job_id:      Uuid;
  kernel_id:   string;          // matches kernels/manifest.toml key
  seed:        ulong;
  params:      [ubyte];         // uniform buffer bytes, MAX 4 KiB
  work_units:  ulong;           // sizer output; kernel-defined meaning
  input_ref:   Hash32;          // null-able
  output_spec: OutputSpec;
  lease_ms:    uint;
  replica_of:  Uuid;            // null-able; set => verification replica
  accumulate:  AccumulationSpec;
}

table GpuLimits {
  max_storage_buffer_binding_size:    ulong;
  max_buffer_size:                    ulong;
  max_compute_workgroups_per_dim:     uint;
  max_compute_invocations_per_group:  uint;
  max_compute_workgroup_storage_size: uint;
}

table WorkerCapabilities {
  kind:            WorkerKind;      // Browser | Native | Mock
  user_agent:      string;
  adapter:         AdapterInfo;     // vendor, architecture, device, backend
  features:        [string];        // "shader-f16", "subgroups", "timestamp-query"
  limits:          GpuLimits;
  supports_webrtc: bool;
}

table TaskStats {
  gpu_ms:       double;   // sum of dispatch durations
  transfer_ms:  double;
  idle_ms:      double;
  dispatches:   uint;
  iterations:   ulong;
  asset_source: AssetSource;   // Cached | Peer | Coordinator | None
}

union Body { Hello, Welcome, BenchmarkRequest, BenchmarkResult, LeaseRequest,
             TaskGrant, LeaseAck, Progress, ResultHeader, Release, Revoke,
             Throttle, PeerList, Signal, Goodbye, Shutdown, Error }

table Envelope { body: Body; }
root_type Envelope;
```

> **R6 reminder.** `DeterminismClass` exists because two *honest* GPUs on different vendors produce different last-ULP results. Never bitwise-compare anything that is not `Exact`.

`TaskStats` is not optional telemetry — it is the input to `EVALUATION.md` §2 (utilization breakdown). Populate every field.

---

## 3. Messages

### Worker → Coordinator

| Message | Fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Hello` | `protocol_version`, `resume_token`, `capabilities` | First message. Version mismatch ⇒ fatal `Error`. |
| `BenchmarkResult` | `kernel_id`, `score`, `samples` | Score in normalized work-units/sec. |
| `LeaseRequest` | `max_tasks` | Pull-based. Worker asks; coordinator decides size. |
| `Progress` | `task_id`, `fraction_done`, `request_renew` | Doubles as heartbeat for that lease. |
| `ResultHeader` | `task_id`, `payload_bytes`, `checksum`, `stats` | Frame carries the payload after the Envelope. |
| `Release` | `task_id`, `reason` | Voluntary give-back. Not a reputation penalty. |
| `Throttle` | `level` (0.0–1.0) | User-set (R7). Coordinator adjusts sizing, does not argue. |
| `Signal` | `to`, `payload` | WebRTC SDP/ICE, relayed. |
| `Goodbye` | `reason` | Clean disconnect; all leases released. |

### Coordinator → Worker

| Message | Fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Welcome` | `worker_id`, `session_token`, `heartbeat_ms`, `kernels` | Token enables reconnect-with-resume. |
| `BenchmarkRequest` | `kernel_id`, `target_ms` | On join; re-sent if throughput drifts. |
| `TaskGrant` | `envelope` | May grant fewer than requested. |
| `LeaseAck` | `task_id`, `expires_at_ms` | Absolute coordinator-clock ms. See §5. |
| `Revoke` | `task_id`, `reason` | Speculative loser, job cancelled, etc. Stop promptly. |
| `PeerList` | `peers` | Candidates for data-plane connections. |
| `Signal` | `from`, `payload` | Relayed WebRTC signaling. |
| `Shutdown` | `reason` | Coordinator going away. |
| `Error` | `code`, `message`, `fatal` | `fatal` ⇒ do not retry with same state. |

### Enums

```
ReleaseReason : UserStopped | TabHidden | DeviceLost | AssetUnavailable | TooSlow | Shutdown
RevokeReason  : SpeculativeLoser | JobCancelled | LeaseExpired | ValidationSuperseded
ErrorCode     : VersionMismatch | UnknownKernel | MalformedMessage | OrphanPayload
              | PayloadTooLarge | ChecksumMismatch | LeaseNotHeld | RateLimited
              | Blacklisted | Internal
```

---

## 4. Invariants

Enforce in `src/protocol/` and assert on both sides. **Every one of these is a length or identity check on attacker-controlled data — treat them as security boundaries, not tidiness (R11).**

1. `params.size() <= 4096` (`kMaxParamsBytes`)
2. `output_spec.bytes <= 8 * 1024 * 1024` (`kMaxOutputBytes`)
3. `fb_len <= kMaxEnvelopeBytes` (64 KiB) — checked before the Verifier runs
4. At most **one** in-flight `ResultHeader` per `task_id` per worker
5. A worker may only `Progress` / `ResultHeader` / `Release` a task it currently holds a lease on ⇒ else `LeaseNotHeld`
6. `replica_of` tasks are never granted to a worker that computed the original or any sibling replica
7. `accumulate.upload_interval_ms >= 500` — more frequent uploads defeat the arithmetic-intensity design (R5)
8. Coordinator never trusts `TaskStats`; telemetry only, never an input to correctness or credit
9. `checksum` is BLAKE3-64 of the payload; mismatch ⇒ discard and requeue, **no reputation penalty** (likely transport corruption, not malice)
10. Asset chunk reassembly: `index < total`, `total == expected_chunks`, and `index * kChunkBytes` computed with checked arithmetic

---

## 5. Clocks, versioning, reconnect

**Clocks.** Never trust worker clocks. `expires_at_ms` is coordinator-clock absolute time; the worker treats it as *"renew before you have consumed `(expires_at - now_at_receipt)` of local elapsed time."* Lease expiry is decided solely by the coordinator.

**Versioning.** `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bumps on any breaking change to the schema or the frame header. Mismatch is fatal with a clear message — no negotiation, no compatibility shims. This is a portfolio project; simplicity beats flexibility.

FlatBuffers' own forward/backward compatibility (append-only fields with defaults) still applies for *additive* changes and does not require a version bump. Removing or reordering a field does.

**Reconnect.** `Welcome.session_token` may be presented in a later `Hello.resume_token`. On successful resume the worker keeps its reputation and benchmark score. It does **not** keep its leases — those expired the moment the connection dropped (R8). Resume is an optimization, never a correctness dependency.

---

## 6. Changing the protocol

1. Edit `protocol/p2pgpu.fbs` only.
2. Rebuild — `flatc` regenerates headers automatically as a CMake build step.
3. Update this file **in the same commit**.
4. Additive field ⇒ no version bump. Removal, reorder, or type change ⇒ bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION` and log a `DECISIONS.md` entry.
5. Add or extend a fuzz seed in `fuzz/corpus/` covering the new shape.

Step 5 is not optional. Every new message shape is new attack surface.
